title: AfterQuery reportedly becomes Y Combinator’s fastest-ever unicorn, now valued at $3.2B
content: AI model-training startup AfterQuery has reportedly raised a round that valued it at $3.2 billion, just five months after announcing its $30 million Series A at a $300 million valuation in April.

title: Open AI’s Astra model is on the way — and very good at breaking into computer systems
content: OpenAI previewed the precautions it is taking as it prepares to release Astra, its newest, cyber-critical LLM.

title: Google’s Android update tackles motion sickness, accessibility, and more
content: While some of the features see Google playing catch-up to Apple, which already offers similar features for iPhone users, others specifically leverage Gemini to provide various improvements.

title: Anthropic’s new Fable release is cheaper, less restrictive
content: Fable 5.1 includes changes meant to reduce token cost and false-positive restrictions from the model's safeguards.

title: Google’s answer to Canva is an AI tool where you prompt instead of design
content: With Google Pics, Google is pushing deeper into the creative software market dominated by Canva and Adobe, but with a distinctly AI-first approach.

title: ChatGPT Health adds Epic integration for clinicians to import patient data
content: OpenAI said that the integration provides read-only access to health records for clinicians.

title: Sequoia-incubated Empirik launches with $21M to predict outages before they happen
content: The startup wants to do for IT infrastructure what Cursor did for software engineering.

title: Amazon Alexa can now alert you when something new might tempt you to shop
content: Amazon is adding a new Alexa-powered feature called “Update Me When” that can send personalized alerts about product launches, tours, books, shows, and other events that could trigger a purchase.

title: AIR raises $50M to help companies vet the skills and add-ons AI agents use
content: AIR's platform can discover agents running at a company, continuously vets any skills and add-ons they use, and blocks any unwanted behavior.

title: Fambot introduces an ‘AI chief of staff’ for families
content: Fambot is building an AI “chief of staff” to help families manage the emails, calendars, school updates, sports schedules, and other logistics of raising kids.

title: Apple shares ‘shocking evidence’ against former employee accused of stealing company data for OpenAI
content: Apple says it has evidence that a former employee destroyed evidence of data theft after learning he was under investigation.

title: The Pentagon now has its own version of ChatGPT and Grok
content: Versions of OpenAI's ChatGPT and SpaceXAI's Grok will join Google's Gemini on the Pentagon's central portal for AI tools.

title: Instagram puts new limits on undisclosed AI profiles
content: As frustration over AI influencers has been growing, Instagram is limiting the reach of undisclosed AI profiles.

title: Harvard Law dropout raises $6M for Blue Voice to build a ‘Harvey for police officers’
content: Blue Voice is trained on department-specific laws, local ordinances, protocols, and guidelines that general-purpose AI tools can't access on the public internet.

title: Clipto uses AI to search terabytes of video and is now valued at $250M
content: The three-year-old startup says it reached $15 million in ARR and profitability before raising its latest $15 million round.

title: Nvidia’s $3.5B MediaTek bet reveals its plan for tackling Big Tech’s AI chip buildout
content: Nvidia invests $3.5 billion into Taiwanese chipmaker MediaTek. The deal shows how Nvidia plans to stay essential to AI infrastructure as Big Tech begins to build its own AI chips.

title: Meeting note-taker Circleback adds a free tier to attract more customers
content: Circleback is also introducing new pricing plans starting from $14 per month.

title: The US is building barriers around drones and robots, but China has scale to get around them
content: The U.S. is shutting out more foreign-made drones and robots. China’s scale means the global competition may simply move elsewhere.

title: Musk’s faster path to more gas turbines comes with pollution problem
content: Elon Musk says a secretive new SpaceX foundry will let him cast his own turbine blades and get gas power online 18 months faster than anyone else — but it's a bet on a fuel source that's already triggering lawsuits and health studies everywhere his (and others') turbines have gone in.

title: Caterpillar is bringing to AI deployment what it learned from automating mining
content: Caterpillar has spent decades putting autonomous machines to work at remote mining sites. It's now bringing that experience to AI deployment.
